event_name: 2025 Kick Off: Coffee With Champions: Small Ball Big Dreams
event_description: Join Negro Leagues Baseball Museum's (NLBM) President Bob Kendrick for a fireside chat with Kansas City Royals Broadcaster Joel Goldberg for a special edition of Coffee With Champions. Joel Goldberg is an Emmy Award-winning and game changing speaker who helps organizations win trust and build championship cultures. To learn more about Joel, please reference here. The $5.00 ticket purchase is a donation to the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum. ABOUT COFFEE WITH CHAMPIONS: Coffee with Champions is a new discussion series developed by the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum (NLBM) in partnership with Starbucks Coffee. Attendees will enjoy an all-star panel of local "community champions" who embody the spirit of the Negro Leagues through their community impact and support of the NLBM. Panelists will share their perspectives on creating a winning culture, leadership and more. The purpose of this program is to provide professional development for emerging leaders, employee resources and affiliated groups in the culturally enriched confines of the NLBM. Coffee and pastries will be provided by Starbucks Coffee. https://youtu.be/mlm4DnRlCSA?si=dZr-C11a0zwNmpDq

event_description: Don’t miss the NLBM‘s 4th Annual “March of the Monarchs celebrating the winning spirit of the great Kansas City Monarchs! Don’t miss the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum‘s (NLBM) 4th Annual “March of the Monarchs,” presented by Evergy starting at12:00 PM, Saturday, May 3rd at the corner of 22nd & Brooklyn (site of Municipal Stadium). It’s a FREE family walk celebrating the winning spirit of the great Kansas City Monarchs and held on the anniversary of Jackie Robinson’s first game with the team (May 6, 1945). The event re-creates the tradition of Monarchs Opening Day when a marching band would lead fans from 18th & Vine to the ballpark at 22nd & Brooklyn. For our celebration, we reverse the route with the walk ending at the NLBM where the celebration will continue with live entertainment, food trucks, mascots, yard games and more.

event_name: Jazz %26amp; Jackie: A Musical Salute to Jackie Robinson
event_description: The Negro Leagues Baseball Museum (NLBM) proudly presents “Jazz & Jackie: A Musical Salute to Jackie Robinson," 8 pm, Saturday, May 24th, 2025 at the Gem Theater in Kansas City, Missouri. Tickets cost $50 (Lower Level) and $35 (Upper Level). A VIP Package cost $100 per person and includes: VIP Seating; pre-event reception at the NLBM; 2 cocktail tickets and an invitation to the opening of the NLBM's new exhibition, "Leaders & Innovators." Limited tickets available! When Jackie Robinson broke Major League Baseball’s color-barrier with the Brooklyn Dodgers in 1947 he not only changed the game but America too. But before Robinson wore number 42 for the Dodgers, he wore number 5 for the Kansas City Monarchs. Jazz & Jackie celebrates his Kansas City professional baseball roots and his unbridled love of jazz, an art form that got its soul in Kansas City. The event features a scintillating concert performance by Dre Scot, with special guest, Smooth Jazz Saxophonist, Jazmin Ghent. JAZZ & JACKIE is made possible through the generous support of the State of Missouri, Republic Services, U.S. Bank, NTDF, Hill's Pet Nutrition, and Evergy. Event proceeds benefit the NLBM. Eventbrite service fees apply.

event_name: 2025 Kansas City Royals Salute to the Negro Leagues
event_description: Join us as we Salute to the Negro Leagues on Sunday, June 29th, at 1:10 p.m. when the Los Angeles Dodgers battle the Royals. The first 15,000 fans through the gates will receive a special Monarchs pin presented by Metropolitan Community College. Both teams will wear custom caps: the Royals will sport a 1945 KC Monarchs road hat, and the Dodgers will wear Brooklyn Dodgers hats, both in the spirit of Jackie Robinson. The 2025 season marks the 80th anniversary of Jackie Robinson’s only season with the Monarchs before debuting for the Brooklyn Dodgers two years later. Starting that day, game-used hats from this game will be auctioned off. Check back for more updates on auction details. Net proceeds will directly benefit the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum. For more information on the 2025 Salute to the Negro Leagues, visit www.mlb.com/royals/tickets/specials/salute-negro-leagues. Starting at 10:30 AM, on Saturday, June 28th, meet the legendary Negro League veterans Pedro Sierra and Sam Allen with paid admission to the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum. Meet and greet details below. Please note due to new 18th Street Pedestrian Mall construction outside of the main entrance to the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum, please be advised vehicles may park at the Soutwest corner of 18th & Paseo Parking Lot. Also, additional free parking can be located in the behind the museum. All museum visitors can walk south on Vine from 17th Terrace; and enter either through the rear entrance or the front entrance of the Museums on 18th Street. Thank you for your patience and understanding at this time.

event_description: Join Us for Coffee with Champions – Summer Series Kickoff!  Join us for the first event in our Coffee with Champions Summer Series, where we’re bringing together Kansas City leaders who are making a difference in our community! Hear inspiring stories and practical advice from local champions who help everyday people thrive and feel empowered. Topics Include: Financial literacy Health and wellness Feeling good inside and out Building a successful business Living with confidence and purpose The $5.00 ticket purchase is a donation to the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum. Please visit the public information here to secure your spot. ABOUT COFFEE WITH CHAMPIONS: Coffee with Champions is a new discussion series developed by the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum (NLBM) in partnership with Starbucks Coffee. Attendees will enjoy an all-star panel of local "community champions" who embody the spirit of the Negro Leagues through their community impact and support of the NLBM. Panelist will share their perspectives on creating a winning culture, leadership and more. The purpose of this program is to provide professional development for emerging leaders, employee resource and affiliated groups in the culturally enriched confines of the NLBM. Coffee and pastries will be provided by Starbucks Coffee. ABOUT NEGRO LEAGUES BASEBALL MUSEUM: The Negro Leagues Baseball Museum (NLBM) is the world’s only museum dedicated to preserving and celebrating the rich history of African American baseball and its impact on the social advancement of America. The privately funded, 501 c3, not-for-profit organization was established in 1990 and is in the heart of Kansas City, Missouri’s Historic 18th & Vine Jazz District. The NLBM operates two blocks from the Paseo YMCA where Andrew “Rube” Foster established the Negro National League in 1920. To learn more about the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum, please visit nlbm.com. https://youtu.be/mlm4DnRlCSA

event_name: 2025 Hall of Game Presented By Hy-Vee
event_description: It's game recognizing game when the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum plays host to the 2025 Hall of Game induction ceremony. The Negro Leagues Baseball Museum (NLBM) today announced that Dusty Baker, Cito Gaston, Willie Randolph, and Jerry Manuel will make up the 2025 Hall of Game Class, presented by Hy-Vee, with Tony Reagins receiving the inaugural JL Wilkinson “Innovator” Award. The distinguished class will be officially inducted in ceremonies on Saturday, October 4th from the Sheraton Crown Center Hotel in Kansas City. “It is my distinct honor to welcome Dusty Baker, Cito Gaston, Willie Randolph and Jerry Manuel to the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum’s Hall of Game and to award Tony Reagins with the JL Wilkinson Innovator Award,” said Bob Kendrick, President of the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum. “They embody the winning spirit and leadership of the Negro Leagues, through their on and off-field endeavors. They are all leaders and innovators who have continued to move the great game of baseball forward while embracing the greats of Black baseball’s past.” Established by the NLBM in 2014, the Hall of Game is a national baseball celebration that annually honors former MLB greats who embodied the spirit and signature style of the Negro Leagues. The 2025 inductees will join baseball greats from the previous classes, which have included some of the game’s biggest and brightest stars such as Roberto Clemente, Joe Morgan, Rickey Henderson, Ozzie Smith, Dave Winfield, Dwight Gooden, the late Dave Parker and Dick Allen amongst a legendary group of others. In addition to the induction ceremony, Hall of Game honorees also will receive permanent recognition as part of the future Buck O’Neil Education and Research Center being developed by the NLBM at the site of the Paseo YMCA, the birthplace of the Negro Leagues. The celebration of African American managers is connected to the museum’s groundbreaking exhibit, entitled “Leaders and Innovators,” that’s on display through March 2026.  2025 Hall of Game VIP Individual Ticket Only Includes: VIP RECEPTION: 5:30 PM DINNER: 6:45 PM PROGRAM & CEREMONY: 8:00 PM 2025 Hall of Game Individual Ticket Only Includes: DINNER: 6:45 PM PROGRAM & CEREMONY: 8:00 PM Ticket Link: 2025 Hall of Game - Negro Leagues Baseball Museum https://youtu.be/pRg45IHX0BE
